co_mchenry_s_peak.blurb: McHenry's Peak is a 13,000-foot summit at the head of Glacier Gorge in Rocky Mountain National Park, reached by hiking past the gorge's string of lakes. It is a serious alpine objective rather than a crag: most of the thirteen climbs here are alpine lines, with a few ice and mixed gullies, one trad route, and some Class 4 and low Class 5 scrambling. Rock climbing runs up to about 5.11, while the winter and spring couloirs reach WI4 with easier mixed pitches. The granite is mostly sound, the lines are long and committing, and afternoon thunderstorms in summer mean an early start. Expect a long day and a long walk out.

co_hully_gully_ice_and_mixed.blurb: Close to Colorado Springs, Hully Gully is a small cold-season venue along the southern rim of South Cheyenne Canyon. It holds two ice pitches that only form in cold, wet years, plus a cluster of drytooling and mixed lines on the walls beside them. Most of the thirteen climbs are mixed, spanning easy M4 up to a few M8 problems, and the ice itself is around WI4. The ice pitches are short, about 40 and 110 feet, which makes the main line a popular place to get a feel for steep ice. Plan on November through early spring, depending on the year's conditions.
co_hully_gully_ice_and_mixed.parking_note: Drive west up Old Stage Road past the Broadmoor Hotel. About 0.6 mile after the hairpin, where the pavement ends, use the large pullout on the right and walk back to the trail, rather than leaving the car on the tight corner where the path begins.

co_andrews_creek_the_gash.blurb: This is a remote winter and spring zone in the upper Andrews Creek valley of Rocky Mountain National Park, beyond The Loch, taking in the basin of The Gash, Andrews Glacier and the south side of Otis Peak. Despite the name there is little reliable ice: the thirteen climbs are mostly mixed routes from M4 to a few M7 and M8 lines, plus some short WI2 ice and steep snow couloirs. Many lines are long, multi-pitch mountain outings. The trail sees little traffic in winter, so expect deep snow, route-finding and a big day out from the Glacier Gorge trailhead.

co_green_thumb.blurb: Above Boulder in the North Flatirons, Green Thumb is a little fin of a tower at the northern tip of the East Ironing Board, well away from the crowded classics. Most of the thirteen routes are short trad cracks, mainly 5.8 to 5.10, with a handful of harder sport lines up to about 5.12 and one aid route. Finger-sized gear is useful on the crack lines. It is reached by a scrambly approach from the saddle near the Third Flatiron, so expect a rougher walk than at the roadside crags and little company.

co_tangen_towers.blurb: Tangen Towers are a pair of small rock towers in the North Flatirons near Boulder, just south of the Fourth Flatiron and a short way off the Royal Arch trail. The lower tower sits nearest the path and the upper one lies directly west of it. Nearly all of the thirteen routes are trad, with one bolted line, and the grades stretch from easy 5.4 up to around 5.12 with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11. Pitches are short, from about thirty to a hundred and sixty feet, and the two-pitch Tangen Tunnel line is the one most people come for. It feels quieter than the big Flatirons faces.

co_ripple_wall.blurb: Ripple Wall is a sandstone cliff of roughly 125 feet in Red Rock Canyon Open Space on the west side of Colorado Springs, just south of Sayer's Wall. It is mainly a sport-climbing wall: eleven bolted routes and two top-rope lines, with grades from about 5.6 to 5.12 and the most from 5.9 to 5.11. The sandstone is gritty and rugged, and the wall is open to the sun with little shade, so cooler days are the best time to visit, and warm days call for an early start and plenty of water. Wide views stretch across the valley.

co_hand_the.blurb: The Hand is a mitten-shaped formation in the Central Flatirons above Boulder, passed on the trail toward Mallory Cave. It is known for a handful of steep sport lines with pockets, crimps and flakes; of its thirteen climbs, nine are sport and four are trad. Difficulty leans hard: most routes sit between 5.11 and 5.13, with one easy 5.4 trad line on the east face as the exception. The faces turned toward the south and west pick up sun from late morning into the afternoon. This is a place for strong sport climbers and for an easy multi-pitch outing.
